A1.evidence: Single complete file, lines 1-1660; all graphics are pixel data (139-214) and text from a bitmap font (53-129); audio is Web Audio (244-310); no external resources, no placeholders.

A2.evidence: result.json: loads_clean true but one pageerror at t=11.2 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading y)'. Cause: killPlayer() line 665 sets game.enemyBullets = [] while updateEnemyBullets (1152-1154) is still iterating the old length by index; the next iteration reads undefined.y. The throw escapes frame() before requestAnimationFrame at 1646, so the loop stops and the game freezes forever. Screenshots 3-after-enter-8s through 4-play-075s are pixel-identical, confirming the freeze.

bugs.text: Console error 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading y)'. killPlayer() replaces game.enemyBullets with [] while updateEnemyBullets is still iterating the old array by index, so the next iteration dereferences undefined. The exception escapes frame() before requestAnimationFrame is re-queued, so the game freezes permanently on the first bullet death whenever another bullet had a lower index. Confirmed: screenshots from 8 s to 75 s are identical.

player.captureTimer is set to 0.8 on capture and never decremented or cleared: resetPlayerForRespawn is never called, killPlayer returns early when the player is already dead, and startGame does not reset it. After one capture the dive scheduler (!p.captureTimer) and the beam catch test are disabled for the rest of the game and the next game, so no enemy ever dives or captures again until a formation bullet kills the player.

Entry-path delay bug: state flips to formation when entryT >= 1 regardless of entryDelay, so groups with delay >= duration appear in place and earlier groups jump mid-path. Most of the formation spawns in place.
Same delay bug on challenge paths: enemies with pathDelay are removed at pathT >= 1 before reaching the end of their curve and vanish in mid-screen.
A tractor Boss teleports from its slot to y=170-185 instead of diving down to the beam position.

Stage badges only record stages numbered exactly 1,5,10,20,30,50; the bottom-right row never shows the arcade decomposition (e.g. stage 7 = 5+1+1) and the current stage's badge appears only after it is cleared.
Captive pull animation moves asymptotically (c.x += (boss.x - c.x) * t * 0.15) and then snaps to the Boss when pulledT reaches 1.
SFX.enemyHit is defined but never called; dead code.
Boss escorts are the first two Goei found in formation, not the Boss's neighbours, and they fly independent dive paths rather than flanking the Boss.

summary: The code is cleanly organised: one state object, a fixed-timestep accumulator loop, separate update and render passes, bitmap font and pixel sprites, and nearly every spec item has a real implementation including the tractor beam, capture, rescue, dual fighter, hostile captive, challenging stages and their scoring. Two engineering slips wreck play: a bullet death reassigns the bullet array inside the loop iterating it and the resulting TypeError kills the requestAnimationFrame chain, so the game freezes for good on the first bullet death (the headless run froze at about 8 s and never recovered); and a capture flag that is never cleared turns off all dives and beams after one capture. Faithfulness is otherwise fair but shallow: enemies mostly pop into formation instead of flying in, the tractor Boss teleports to its beam position, challenge paths are single S-curves whose late enemies vanish early, escorts do not fly with the Boss, badges are not decomposed, and explosions are a generic radial burst. It looks like Galaga on the title and formation screens, but it does not survive its own first death.
